subject: QBR inputs: infra capacity planning & unit-econ numbers (GPU spend, util, batching)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR inputs: infra capacity planning & unit-econ numbers (GPU spend, util, batching)

Team —

As part of the upcoming QBR I need consolidated numbers and a short narrative (1-2 bullets) on implications for our capacity/financial ask. Specifically we need: 

- YTD GPU spend (hosted + dedicated) and month-by-month trend for Q1 2026.
- Current and peak GPU utilization (7/14/30-day windows) and any known outlier workloads.
- Estimated unit economics impact from batching and KV/prefix caching (current measured delta if available, and conservative projection if we roll out the new caching policy).
- Two capacity scenarios for Q2: a base case (no reserve purchases), and a committed case (reserved capacity + negotiated pricing). For each scenario include the expected latency implications and a short risk note.

Attachments: I pulled the infra dashboard snapshot for Q1 so you can reference existing dashboards. Please return numbers as a single-sheet CSV or spreadsheet and 2–3 bullet takeaways by EOD 2026-03-01 so I can incorporate into the leadership slide deck.

Attach: [Attachment: redwood-infra-dashboard-2026Q1.pdf (pdf)]

Why this matters: execs want a crisp ask and the unit-econ picture – show whether a committed purchase materially lowers per-token cost and if batching/caching improvements give us runway without extra capacity.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product & Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR inputs: infra capacity planning & unit-econ numbers (GPU spend, util, batching)

Laura —

Quick pass with the infra numbers attached. High level:

- YTD GPU spend (hosted + dedicated): $4.6M (Jan: $1.5M, Feb: $1.6M, Mar est: $1.5M extrapolated). Detailed monthly churn in attached CSV.
- Utilization: running average utilization (30d): 62%; 14d: 68%; 7d: 74%. Peak burst windows on 2026-02-12 and 2026-02-20 due to large customer rerank batch jobs (these are external-origin jobs).
- Batching & caching impact: from our A/B in prod, enabling KV prefix caching + tighter batching window yields a measured token-cost reduction of ~11% for chat/generation workloads, with median p50 latency increase <5ms. Conservative rollout projection: 6–8% cost reduction platform-wide when rolled out with current autoscaler settings.
- Capacity scenarios: 
  * Base case (no new reserves): expect continued spot/backfill at 70–80% utilization; latency SLOs hold but risk of throttling in 99p during peak bursts.
  * Committed case (buying 150 GPUs reserved across us-west): reduces per-GPU cost by ~18% on the committed portion; combined with caching the blended per-token cost reduction is ~22% vs current. Latency improves for majority steady-state traffic; tail risk remains for large batch reranks unless we keep some burst buffer (recommend +10% burst pool).

Notes & blockers:
- The forecasting assumes current request mix; if we onboard two new large embedding customers in Q2 that we are tracking, these numbers shift materially.
- We need procurement/finance signoff to start lock-in conversations — attaching a simple model.

Attached: gpu-utilization-summary.csv

Adding product context —

- Usage mix: steady gen/chat is ~58% of token volume, embeddings 30%, rerank/batch jobs 12%. Reranks create high-variance tail events and often run without prefix caching which increases KV pressure.
- Batching window: our current default (60ms) prioritizes latency, but if we expand to 80–120ms for low-priority routes we estimate another 4–6% batch-related cost savings for those routes with minimal user-facing latency impact. We should mark which routes are allowed to have extended batching.
- OKR nodal alignment: this ties to Infra cost-savings OKR and Product reliability OKR. I propose we own a small experiment in week 1 of Q2 to flip caching policy for 10% of traffic and measure rollup. If results align with Vivek's A/B we can accelerate rollout and include the expected delta in the QBR ask.

CC: quick heads-up that expanding batching without throttling changes will push more load into our autoscaler; Vivek please call out if that requires config changes.

Dev
Principal PM, Serving
Redwood Inference
